claims: As of April 2026, the total U.S. gross national debt exceeds $39 trillion.
The U.S. Treasury manages the debt through the sale of securities including T-bills, notes, and bonds.
Projections indicate the U.S. gross national debt could exceed 125% of GDP this year.
The U.S. debt is measured by the total outstanding borrowing.
The U.S. debt is roughly divided into debt held by the public (~$31 trillion) and intragovernmental debt (~$7.5 trillion).
The U.S. Department of the Treasury issues debt to finance government operations.
Congress manages the U.S. debt through a legal debt ceiling.
The U.S. debt ceiling has been raised numerous times.
About 15% of the federal budget is currently used for interest payments on the U.S. debt.
The U.S. debt is currently at its highest level relative to the economy since World War II.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects global public debt could reach 99% of world GDP by 2028.
The U.S. national debt is increasing by approximately $7−8 billion per day.
The U.S. national debt is increasing by over $87,000 per second.
The U.S. debt per household is approximately $289,204.
The U.S. Treasury provides a daily tracker of the total outstanding public debt.
The total outstanding public debt can be viewed in the U.S. Treasury's Debt to the Penny dataset.
